headline: High: MemMachine’s MCP and broad network egress can feed social-auto-upload with unverified content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; shared-data leakage is limited but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so its outputs can be bridged into social-auto-upload workflows. social-auto-upload uses CLI/headless automation and can act on supplied content. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this above medium: an attacker-controlled MemMachine output could be treated as instructions or metadata by the uploader.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into social-auto-upload command arguments or templates
IF the uploader parses MemMachine text as captions, prompts, or instructions
IF an MCP bridge forwards untrusted content without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a manual review step before passing MemMachine output onward
Wrap MemMachine output in a fixed schema and reject free-form instructions
Disable any automation that consumes raw text from MemMachine
Use provenance labels on all cross-agent payloads
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while social-auto-upload touches account data and uploads media over broad network egress. There is no shared filesystem or direct evidence of automatic data transfer, but if MemMachine content is forwarded into upload metadata or logs, sensitive context can leak to a third-party platform. The pathway exists but is not default-proven.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is included in captions, descriptions, or tags
IF social-auto-upload logs received prompts or metadata to remote services
IF both agents are run under the same account and share exported artifacts
mitigations: Strip personal facts before handoff
Review upload metadata for sensitive text
Keep agent logs local and short-retention
Use separate accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: add redaction before network transmission

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable local resources, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable API not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable remote account or API token
IF an external orchestrator serializes their actions onto one shared resource
IF MemMachine is extended with write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable destinations
Serialize actions through one operator queue
Check for hidden write scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared remote resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can generate conversational context and long-term preferences, and social-auto-upload can execute uploads to external platforms. If the uploader treats MemMachine output as authoritative captions, tags, or scheduling instructions, a mistaken or injected suggestion can cascade into a public post. The pairwise handoff is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes MemMachine-generated text without verification
IF MemMachine output is used to choose upload targets or timing
IF no human approval exists before posting
mitigations: Require human approval before posting
Compare MemMachine output against a fixed checklist
Limit MemMachine to drafting only
Log the source of every uploaded field
requires-engineering: add validation gates before publish

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media to external social platforms. That creates a plausible retention and disclosure mismatch if MemMachine-derived personal data is republished or retained longer than intended. No residency or certification data is provided, so I cannot justify high severity; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine-derived personal data is copied into social-auto-upload metadata or captions
IF uploaded content is retained by the platform longer than the source policy allows
IF deletion requests are handled in one system but not the other
mitigations: Avoid sending personal facts into upload metadata
Set short retention on MemMachine logs
Document deletion/export handling for both systems
Review platform privacy settings before posting
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
